clue.text: One preserving gap made by engineer in mineral

indicators.note: the engineer's abbreviation is placed inside the word for the mineral

parts.note: spar is a crystalline mineral, as in feldspar
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer working in a quarry somehow keeps a gap open in the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacer is a piece inserted to keep a set distance between two parts.

clue.text: Publicity man has no time to discuss with governor

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer

indicators.note: the time letter is removed from the word for discuss

parts.note: to consult is to discuss with someone

explanation.surface: A press officer is too busy to talk things over with the governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A proconsul was a governor of a Roman province.

clue.text: Officer has dead to collect and sort out

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: After a battle an officer must gather and identify the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather material together and arrange it in order.

clue.text: Scrap paper

definitions.meaning: a scrap of cloth, a remnant

explanation.surface: A piece of waste paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is both a scrap of cloth and a slang word for a low-quality newspaper.

clue.text: Going to bed, or getting dressed again'

definitions.meaning: ... for the night means going off to sleep

explanation.surface: Someone is either heading to bed or putting their clothes back on.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring is the ordinary word for going to bed, and split as re-tiring it means dressing (attiring) again.

clue.text: Animal deliberately concealed

indicators.note: the animal sits hidden among the letters of the clue word

explanation.surface: Some creature has been purposely kept out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, an African and Asian mammal.

clue.text: Unpolluted river flowing round resort -— managed to' get over

indicators.note: the river's course runs round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river

indicators.note: in a down clue, managed is placed over, above, the resort

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A clean river winds past a spa town, and someone gets across it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get over' places one piece above the other, as this is a down clue; the river's name is split after its first letter to wrap them.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent water is clear, so free of pollution.

clue.text: In excitement of big race, one protects one's heart

indicators.note: excited letters jump about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A horse's heart pounds during the thrill of a big race.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribs form a bony cage round the chest that shields the heart and lungs.

clue.text: Opera expected to be short

indicators.note: the word for expected is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: normal means usual, as expected

explanation.surface: An opera that is expected to be brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's opera about a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Night-bird seen in day a disappointment

indicators.note: the bird is spotted sitting inside the word for day

parts.note: light, as in daylight, stands for the day
the owl is the classic bird of the night

explanation.surface: Spotting an owl in daytime is a let-down for the birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A lowlight is the worst or most disappointing moment, the opposite of a highlight.

clue.text: Red and gold are blazing

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to burn is to be blazing

explanation.surface: A fire of red and gold flames is burning brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown shade, used especially of hair.

clue.text: In brief, a centre of population

definitions.text: In brief, a centre of population

parts.words: In brief, a centre of population
parts.note: a large city whose name is usually shortened to two letters, LA

explanation.surface: A summary statement about where people are concentrated.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian city is a major population centre, known for short as LA.

clue.text: In Channel, Force 4 as an example

parts.note: a gutter is a channel for rainwater
to press is to force

explanation.surface: A weather forecast for the English Channel gives wind at Force 4.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is the answer to 4 Down, RAG, a slang word for a trashy newspaper. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is one example of sensationalist tabloid journalism.

clue.text: Panic, losing end of wing

indicators.note: the word for panic drops its final letter

parts.note: alarm is a state of panic

explanation.surface: A bird panics after losing the tip of a wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alar is an adjective meaning relating to wings, from Latin ala, wing.

clue.text: It was full of noises I shall hear

indicators.note: the contraction for the two words is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: contracted, I shall becomes I'll

explanation.surface: Someone says they will listen to a noisy place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Caliban in Shakespeare's The Tempest: 'the isle is full of noises'.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest Prospero's island is described by Caliban as full of noises.

clue.text: Read threat to blow up Pyramids

indicators.note: blowing something up scatters its pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a terrorist's threat to blow up the Pyramids of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetrahedra are triangular pyramids, solids with four triangular faces.

clue.text: Drink' regularly offered by Telegraph

indicators.note: every third letter of the newspaper name is taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A cuppa is routinely provided by the Telegraph newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Take letters 1, 4 and 7 of Telegraph. The Daily Telegraph is a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the classic British hot drink.

clue.text: Firm totters, causing a bit of a stink

parts.note: rocks means sways or totters

parts.words: causing a bit of a stink
parts.note: olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A company wobbles and creates a minor scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock-solid means completely firm and unshakable.

clue.text: Extremely sane, holding on to silver that's very popular

indicators.note: the phrase for sane wraps round and keeps hold of the silver symbol

parts.note: all there is an informal way of saying fully sane
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A perfectly sensible person clings to their silver, which everyone wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all the rage is fashionable and in great demand at present.

clue.text: In lake, start to angle to port

indicators.note: the opening letter goes in the word for lake

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone at a lake begins fishing off the left side of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Taranto is a southern Italian seaport.

clue.text: Creature irresponsibly passed

definitions.meaning: a male deer or rabbit is called this
in the idiom 'pass the ...' this is handed on to dodge responsibility

explanation.surface: An animal was carelessly handed along.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male deer, and passing the buck means shifting blame irresponsibly.

clue.text: Singer flags

definitions.meaning: a songbird of the finch-like family
festive flags and streamers strung up for decoration

explanation.surface: A vocalist is tiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunting is a small songbird and also decorative strings of flags.

clue.text: Spare place 'setting not wanted at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for a place setting is dropped

parts.note: a cover is a single place laid at a dining table

explanation.surface: An extra place laid at the table proves unnecessary to start with.
explanation.definitionFit: Over can mean left over or spare, as in food that is over after a meal.

clue.text: Sebastian's sister takes a bow

definitions.meaning: Sebastian's twin in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
a stringed instrument played with a bow

explanation.surface: A performer's sister steps forward for applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Twelfth Night and an instrument bowed like a violin.

clue.text: Dreadfully prim, aunt is: her creed?

indicators.note: done dreadfully, the words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A severe aunt lives by a strict, joyless moral code.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritanism is a strict moral outlook, the kind of creed a prim aunt might hold.

clue.text: Drive back as sick man needs picking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a leper is a man with leprosy

explanation.surface: Someone is told to push back because an ill person needs collecting.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back an attacker or force.

clue.text: Black cat --. what dead one may do?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A black cat is mentioned, then a joke about whether a dead one can rebound.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud cheque bounces, coming back unpaid, so a dead one may do this.

clue.text: Item on page, only a small piece

indicators.note: the item word is placed on, following, the page letter

parts.note: an article is an item, as in an article of clothing

explanation.surface: A news item on a page turns out to be only a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny fragment or bit of matter.

clue.text: Resistance to small coin? It's current

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
1p, a one-penny coin, with the one written as I

explanation.surface: A physics puzzle about resisting a small coin and electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip is a strong current in the sea, as in a rip tide.

clue.text: Excitement going to clubs for rave

indicators.note: the excitement word goes to, after, the card-suit letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
arousal is a state of excitement

explanation.surface: Thrill-seekers head to nightclubs for a wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a noisy drinking party, a rave in the old sense of a wild celebration.

clue.text: Make space about a place of worship

indicators.note: the word for space goes about, around, the verb for make

parts.note: a pad is a place or space, as in a launch pad or one's own pad
to make for somewhere is to go there

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear room around a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a temple in Buddhist countries.
